root_idea.summary: The supplied lexical evidence centers on a minute feature of a date stone and its figurative value as an emblem of utter insignificance.
root_idea.development: Concrete date-stone referents such as a trace, membrane, cleft, or germ-point are extended figuratively to the idea of possessing only a negligible amount, or nothing of consequence.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested nominal is a distinct lexical item; the public headword is normalized to its classical citation form قِطْمِير.

senses.definition: The slight trace or thin membrane on the back of a date stone.
senses.usage_conditions: In 35:13, this minute date-stone remnant is invoked as the least conceivable possession.

senses.definition: A negligible amount or paltry possession; anything of no appreciable consequence.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction concerning what others possess besides God, it denotes not even the smallest share, by reference to the minute date-stone membrane.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cleft or split in a date stone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete date-stone sense distinct from the thin outer membrane and the germ-point.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The thin integument or skin on a date stone, between the stone and the date flesh; the part called فُوفَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete botanical or anatomical referent of the date stone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The white point or germ in the back of a date stone, from which the palm grows when planted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete germinal feature of the date stone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression مَا أَصَبْتُ مِنْهُ قِطْمِيرًا, to obtain nothing from someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional negated expression using the sense of a paltry or negligible amount.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The unit's concrete date-stone branches are represented under the Quranic trace sense and the distinct classical referents.
The unit's paltry-thing Quranic use and its negated idiom are represented separately.

cautions: Lane records قِطْمَارٌ as a variant alongside قِطْمِيرٌ; the Quran-attested form and public headword are قِطْمِير.
Lane's printed Quran citation in this entry uses historical notation and is not treated as an independently derived modern verse location; the supplied QAC occurrence is 35:13.
